messages.content: Solve word problems step by step.
Train A leaves city X at 60 km/h heading east. Train B leaves city Y (300 km east) at 80 km/h heading west, 30 minutes later. When and where do they meet?

message.content:
<think>We need to parse the problem: Two trains, Train A leaves city X at 60 km/h heading east. Train B leaves city Y (300 km east) at 80 km/h heading west, 30 minutes later. So Train A starts at t=0 from X heading east. Train B starts from Y (which is 300 km east of X) heading west, i.e., towards X, but starts 30 minutes (0.5 hour) later. So they are moving towards each other. We need to find when and where they meet.

We can set up coordinate system: Let X be at position x=0. Y is at x=300 km. Train A moves east, i.e., increasing x. Train B moves west, i.e., decreasing x. Train A speed v_A = 60 km/h. Train B speed v_B = 80 km/h.

Train A position as a function of time t (in hours) after its departure: x_A(t) = 60 t.

Train B starts at t = 0.5 h after Train A's start. So at time t (global time), B's travel time is (t - 0.5) if t >= 0.5, else B hasn't started. B's position: x_B(t) = 300 - 80 (t - 0.5) = 300 - 80 t + 40 = 340 - 80 t. (Check: At t=0.5, x_B = 340 - 80*0.5 = 340 - 40 = 300, correct.)

They meet when x_A(t) = x_B(t). Solve: 60 t = 340 - 80 t => 60 t + 80 t = 340 => 140 t = 340 => t = 340/140 = 34/14 = 17/7 ≈ 2.428571... hours after Train A's departure.

Thus meeting occurs at t = 2.428571... hours after Train A left. That's about 2 hours + 0.428571*60 = 2 hours + 25.714 minutes ≈ 2 hours 25 minutes 43 seconds. Actually 0.428571 hour = 0.428571*60 = 25.714 minutes = 25 minutes and 0.714*60 = 42.857 seconds ≈ 43 seconds. So meeting time: approx 2h 25m
